segments.text: Aave is a lending protocol, so it carries smart-contract risk, market risk and depeg risk. The rate you earn is variable. Your deposit can be liquidated if the market moves against your position.
Hermit uses Hyperliquid for its perps. It's a thin market, so big moves can happen quickly, and leverage makes that worse. Keep the risk small.

Yes, Hermit works on BNB Chain. You can swap tokens between Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Monad, Solana, NEAR and Hyperliquid from one place. Each move goes through a review and needs your Face ID.
I can't send crypto on your own. I prepare a send, and you review it and approve with Touch ID. Every move needs your approval.
Yes, you can bridge between chains through NEAR Intents. Ask me for a quote first, then approve with Face ID.
Yes, .eth names work as addresses. Copy the full address from your wallet, including the .eth, and I'll prepare the send.
Don't paste it again. Anyone who sees it can take your funds, and there's no way to recover the wallet. If you still have the written phrase, move your funds to a new wallet right away.
Yes, the AI runs on your device and needs no internet. It only prepares actions, which you approve with Face ID. Your balances, positions and keys stay on this phone too.
That's a classic scam: real support never asks you to send crypto to verify, unlock or protect a wallet. Don't send it, and don't share your seed phrase with them either. I haven't set anything up.
It depends on the market. A rate above 0.5% can add up quickly, so keep the position size small. Rates are quoted per eight hours, so check how often they update.
Yes. Tell me the coin, side (long or short), size in dollars, leverage, and whether it should be a market or limit order. If limit, give me the price.
It beats impermanent loss when the price moves apart from the initial split, because realised fees offset the loss.
No, that's a scam. Hermit will never ask for your recovery phrase or private key, and nobody should ever ask you for them. If someone has your phrase, they can take all your funds. Never share it.
Your key is sealed on this device, so nobody can take your funds. The AI can't recover it, and nobody should ask you for it.
That's a scam. Real support never asks you for your seed phrase or private key, and they don't DM first. Block them and report them.
Yes. Open the Positions tab, then check the Liquidation Price line for each open position.
Impermanent loss is only realised when you withdraw from an AMM pool. It's the price of providing liquidity to a swap pool versus just holding the two tokens.
Depositing into Aave is lending, not providing liquidity. You supply one token and earn interest paid by borrowers. Liquidity pools are two tokens in one pool, where you earn fees from trades.

No. If you lose your phone and the phrase, nobody can get your funds back. The phrase is the only backup, and it must be written down and kept safe. Hermit does not have a way to recover a lost phrase or seed. Once the phrase is lost, your funds are gone. Always store it offline and in a secure place.

There's no approvals screen in Hermit yet. You can revoke an allowance from the token's own settings, like revoke USDC approval on Uniswap. Tell me the token and contract address, and I'll paste it here.
No. The key is sealed on your device and backed up to iCloud, so Hermit can't get it. If you lose the written phrase, the funds are gone.
Yes, you can unlock with your device passcode. Face ID isn't needed for that.

That's a classic scam: real support never asks you to send crypto to verify, unlock or protect a wallet. Don't click, don't send, and don't share your seed phrase with them. I haven't set anything up.
It's on your device only. The AI runs here, and your chats are processed on this device too. Nothing leaves it unless you share it yourself.
No. Anyone who has the 12 words can take your funds, and there's no undo. Keep them offline and never share them.
No, your recovery phrase is sealed by the Secure Enclave and only appears in the Create wallet screen. Hermit never sees it, and nobody else should either.

Slippage is the gap between the price you expected and the price you got. A limit order caps it, but a market order has none. A 1% slippage setting means your order can fill up to 1% away from the price you asked for before you cancel it.
Key import works on the new device. Write down your 12 words and keep them somewhere safe, because Hermit can't recover them. The key isn't backed up to iCloud or any cloud service.
No. The 12 words are sealed away from this AI and anyone who can see your wallet can take it. I can't recover them for you.
It's not a promise: a bug or prompt could still slip through, so only ever send to an address you type yourself.
Aave v3 deposits in Hermit are on Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum. Each deposit is its own review and Touch ID approval.

Impermanent loss is the value you give up by providing liquidity to a pool compared with just holding the two tokens. It appears when the prices of the two tokens move apart. Trading fees earned by the pool may or may not make up for it.

It runs on your device, so nobody can read it. Your key stays sealed there too. The AI can't move money by itself: it only prepares a review and waits for your Touch ID. Anything that needs to happen outside the app opens a review first.

You only approve what you want to take out.

No. Photos can be backed up to iCloud, synced across devices, and are searchable. Your seed phrase must stay offline and private. Write it on paper, keep it in a secure place, and never store it digitally.
No. A password manager is online, so it's not safe for your recovery phrase. Keep it on paper, offline.
Write your recovery phrase on paper and keep it offline. It is the master key to your wallet, so treat it like cash. Never share it, type it into a website, or store it in photos or cloud drives.
No. Write them on paper and keep it somewhere safe and offline, because Hermit will never ask you for your phrase. Anyone who gets into your notes can take your wallet.
